newsitem.title: UK: British MP proposes Holocaust law.
newsitem.headline: British MP proposes Holocaust law.

text.p: British members of parliament on Wednesday backed a new law under which denying the Holocaust took place would be a criminal offence.
They supported a bid by Labour Party legislator Michael Gapes to introduce a bill to ban suggestions that German World War Two leader Adolf Hitler never moved to exterminate the Jews.
The bill has no chance of making progress through parliament ahead of an imminent general election.
But Labour leader Tony Blair, who is favourite to become Prime Minister after the poll, said there was a "very strong case" for such a law.
Gapes told parliament many European countries had outlawed the denial of the Holocaust, including Germany and Austria. But in Britain attempts to prosecute people came to nothing.

"Survivors of the Holocaust, relatives of those who died in the Holocaust and many other people....find it unbelievable that that loophole in our current legislation is remaining in existence," he said.
Blair backed Gapes in a speech in London when he opened an exhibition on Anne Frank, the Dutch Jewish teenager who kept a diary of her wartime experiences.
"There is a very strong case that denial of the Holocaust should be a specific offence," he said. "We are giving active consideration to how this should be achieved."
But David Irving, a British historian who disputes that six million Jews died in the Holocaust, said the proposed bill was an offensive assault on free speech.
"I want to be able to ask "was it six million or was it two million?'" he said. "It seems very unhealthy to be barred from holding an opinion."
